stories.headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue, airports and oil sites targeted
stories.what_happened: Yemen's Houthis have attacked Saudi airports and Aramco sites since early October after a UN-brokered truce collapsed.
stories.why_it_matters: Airport and oil attacks put people at risk and disrupt travel and energy supplies.

key_facts.fact: Saudi civil aviation authorities reported at least 20 deaths and 356 injuries from Houthi attacks on airports between October 6 and 11.
The deadliest strike hit Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on October 10, killing at least 12 people, including an American citizen.
Other airports hit include Dammam, Abha, Jazan and Najran.
The Houthi leader set out an 'airports for airports, ports for ports, and a blockade for a blockade' policy after Sanaa's airport was hit.
The Saudi-backed Yemeni government said the Sanaa strike was meant to stop an Iranian plane from landing there.
A UN-brokered truce in place since 2022 collapsed.
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile launched toward Riyadh.

The Bab el-Mandeb strait is the southern exit of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia, and its importance has grown because the Iran conflict has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.
Who controls the strait is disputed: a Reuters-based report said the Houthis had taken it, while pro-government forces claim to have secured it.
The Houthis announced a blockade of Saudi vessels passing through the waterway.

stories.headline: Attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz keep oil above $100
stories.what_happened: Iran has attacked tankers in the Strait of Hormuz; Brent crude has traded around $105 to $110 a barrel.
stories.why_it_matters: Oil fuels transport and industry, so higher prices raise costs for households.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude was about $107.83 and WTI about $97.07 on 16 October 2026 in one market analysis; another put Brent at $105.48.
Brent hit a session high of $110 a barrel after Iran escalated attacks in the strait, reports said.
UK officials have reported at least nine attacks in the waterway so far in October (Yahoo Finance).
Global fuel prices began climbing this spring after the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, closing the Strait of Hormuz.

Kpler put average oil clearance through Hormuz at 11.62 million barrels a day in the seven days ending 13 October, against a baseline of 17.15 million, and linked the drop to increased Iranian military activity.
Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz were reported at a high in October (SAFETY4SEA headline: 'attacks reach record high in October').

stories.headline: Russia strikes all three of Kyiv's heat and power plants
stories.what_happened: A Russian ballistic missile barrage hit Kyiv's three combined heat and power plants overnight 13-14 October.
stories.why_it_matters: Winter is near and people depend on power and heating.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said all three of Kyiv's combined heat and power plants came under attack; everyone was evacuated and nobody was injured there.
Zelenskyy said Russian strikes had caused significant damage to 26 energy sites and at least 600,000 people were without power.
Trump had announced an 'energy ceasefire'; Zelenskyy said Russia kept striking energy sites, and the Kremlin's Peskov said only 'Contacts are ongoing'.

stories.headline: Student protests in Albania spread to a third day
stories.what_happened: Students in Tirana protested over university conditions and demanded PM Edi Rama resign; a fire broke out at the Education Ministry.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how young people press governments over schooling and jobs.

key_facts.fact: Protests entered a third day; demonstrators broke into the Education Ministry overnight and lit a fire, police said, with 16 arrests; police used tear gas and water cannon.
Students cited university conditions, higher education costs, lack of financial support and employment prospects.
Rama's Socialist Party holds a parliamentary majority after winning a fourth consecutive term last year.

Reuters reported that the Education Ministry caught fire on Wednesday during student protests over corruption and education; police used tear gas and water cannon, and a nearby Raiffeisen Bank branch also caught fire.
Deputy Prime Minister Albana Kociu said on Facebook that protest is a legitimate right but cannot be an excuse for violence.

stories.headline: US inflation rose to 3.7% in September on costlier gasoline
stories.what_happened: Consumer prices rose 0.6% from August to September; annual inflation 3.7%, up from 3.4%.
stories.why_it_matters: Prices affect every household and may push the Fed to raise rates.

key_facts.fact: The September CPI report, released October 14, 2026, showed inflation at 3.7% year over year, up from 3.4% in August, with gasoline as the main driver.
Consumer prices rose 0.6% from August to September, the biggest monthly gain in five months.
Core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 2.6% in September from a year ago, up from 2.4% the previous month.
The Fed's next meeting is Oct. 27-28.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear opposition plea on voter-list revision on 27 October
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court linked Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders' petition on the Election Commission's special intensive revision (SIR) of voter lists to another case; both are to be heard on October 27.
stories.why_it_matters: Voter lists decide who can vote.

key_facts.fact: The petition seeks an independent audit, protection for eligible voters and a temporary halt to the revision.
The Supreme Court linked the petition to another pending case and both are to be heard on October 27.
The Supreme Court has issued notice but has not delivered a final judgment.

stories.headline: Delhi Police end Jantar Mantar as a protest site, name three new venues
stories.what_happened: A Delhi Police standing order dated 11 October removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and named Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi instead.
stories.why_it_matters: Where people may protest is part of how citizens can voice disagreement.

key_facts.fact: The order, by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and dated October 11, names Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground, East Delhi as replacement venues.
The order says it follows the recommendations of a committee set up by the Union Home Ministry.
Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib has approached the Delhi High Court; police told the court the decision was based on a Supreme Court order of October 9.
A separate plea challenging the standing order is pending before the Supreme Court.
Cockroach Janta Party leaders were detained near Jantar Mantar after trying to enter.

stories.headline: Webb telescope data reveal the lopsided atmosphere of the planet WASP-17b
stories.what_happened: A Cornell-led team published in Nature Astronomy on October 14 a map of the uneven edge of WASP-17b's atmosphere using JWST data.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how astronomers study far-off worlds.

key_facts.fact: The team used a technique called transmission strings, measuring the distance from the planet's centre to its atmospheric edge at many points.
The atmosphere reaches farther on the evening side, while the cooler morning side is less extended; winds carry heat from the day side to the night side.
Water and carbon dioxide were distributed fairly consistently around the atmospheric edge.
WASP-17 is roughly 1,300 light-years away per Cornell and Bristol.

A 2023 Webb (MIRI) study reported silica (quartz) crystal clouds in WASP-17b's atmosphere, the first time a specific cloud species was identified in a transiting exoplanet, according to Advanced Science News/Cornell.
ESA published an image of Webb spotting quartz crystals in the clouds of WASP-17b in October 2023.

stories.headline: World's first self-stabilising nuclear clock runs for over a day in Vienna
stories.what_happened: TU Wien and PTB built a thorium-229 nuclear clock whose laser corrects itself; published in Nature.
stories.why_it_matters: Better clocks help navigation and tests of physics.

key_facts.fact: A thorium-229 crystal serves as the timing reference, driven by a laser; the system detects and corrects frequency shifts automatically.
The prototype ran for over 24 hours with no outside adjustment.
Precision was about 10^-15, roughly one second in 30 million years; it still trails the best optical atomic clocks.
The work was led by Thorsten Schumm and Ekkehard Peik.

stories.headline: A strong El Nino is quieting the Atlantic hurricane season
stories.what_happened: NOAA gave a 75% chance of a below-normal Atlantic season and a 90% chance of a strong or very strong El Nino in Aug-Oct.
stories.why_it_matters: El Nino changes weather worldwide.

key_facts.fact: NOAA's August update put the chance of a below-normal season at 75%, up from 55% in May, forecasting 7 to 13 named storms, 2 to 6 hurricanes and 0 to 2 major hurricanes.
NOAA gave a 90% chance of a strong or very strong El Nino during August, September and October.
El Nino raises upper-level winds over the Atlantic, which disrupts storm development.
NOAA's administrator said 'it only takes one' storm.

stories.headline: Saudi league moves three matches
stories.what_happened: Al Nassr v Al Ahli moved to March 6, 2027; two other games to December 19.
stories.why_it_matters: Sport is disrupted by the conflict.

key_facts.fact: The Saudi Pro League moved Al Nassr's clash with Al Ahli to March 6, 2027; two other matchweek nine games moved to December 19.
The league cited 'logistical considerations' about the minimum rest period between matches, not security.
Al Nassr beat Uzbekistan's Neftchi 3-1 in the AFC Champions League Elite on Monday after a delayed start due to a threat of missile attacks from Yemen's Houthis.
